open_points.subject: Randomly minted entity identifiers
open_points.text: `trial_execution_id` M07, `binding_id` M11, `run_id` M19, `approval_id` M24 and `grant_id` M25 are minted at random by the kernel; one that already exists is minted again.
open_points.question: Which module owns generating these identifiers and retrying collisions atomically with record creation?
options: `store` mints every random identifier inside the record-writing transaction
Each domain module (`functions`, `bindings`, `runs`, `effects`) mints the identifiers for its records and `store` only detects collisions
A separate lower-level identifier capability owns minting and collision retry
open_points.default_guess: Have `store` mint and collision-check every random identifier inside the transaction that creates the record.

open_points.subject: File digest and size facts
open_points.text: `content_digest`, `size_bytes`; `store` owns "publishing a file only complete and digest-checked", while trial file outputs keep "digest, size and media type, no bytes".
open_points.question: Which module computes the authoritative digest and size for spooled files, trial fixtures and ephemeral trial file outputs, and which modules merely verify or record those facts?
options: `canonical_values` owns hashing raw file bytes; producers compute through it and `store` verifies
`store` computes facts for persisted files while `sandbox` computes them independently for trial outputs
Each producing module computes its own file facts
open_points.default_guess: Give `canonical_values` one raw-byte digest operation, let producing modules call it, and let `store` independently verify persisted bytes.

open_points.subject: Manifest instance validation
open_points.text: `bindings` owns "proposal checks in their fixed order" including instance address and required-header checks, while `service_invoker` owns "the pre-send checks of the instance and the inputs (A09 rule 6)" and `prepare_request` "owns every instance failure".
open_points.question: Which module owns the shared predicates for validating an instance URL and its required headers, so proposal/acceptance checks and pre-send checks cannot implement them differently?
options: `service_invoker` owns reusable instance-validation capabilities that `bindings` calls
`bindings` owns instance validation and passes a validated result to `service_invoker`
The two modules intentionally implement the same predicates independently
open_points.default_guess: Make `service_invoker` own reusable pure instance-validation capabilities and have `bindings` call them during proposal, acceptance and startup checks.
